images.img1Desc: A woman in a purple jacket walks along a path through a green forest. Tall tree trunks, moss-covered rocks and a fallen tree surround her, and sunlight comes through the leaves.
images.img2Desc: A dirty river runs through waste ground, full of rubbish and plastic. Old containers and barrels lie on the cracked, dry earth beside it. Factory chimneys behind release smoke, and there are yellow warning signs on the right.
images.pairBoth: Both photos show an outdoor environment.
images.pairDiff: The first shows clean, healthy nature, the second a badly polluted place.

questions.prompt: Do you enjoy spending time in nature?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like park. Trees are nice.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like nature. I like to walk in the park and see the trees. It is good because it is quiet. I like the flowers.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I enjoy spending time in nature. I think it's very relaxing. For example, I like to go for walks in the forest near my house. It's nice to get away from the city. However, sometimes there are too many bugs!
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I absolutely love it. There's nothing quite like getting away from the city for a while. Whenever I get the chance, I head off to the countryside to clear my head. The fresh air and quiet really help me unwind, and I always come back feeling completely recharged.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men tabiatni yaxshi ko'raman. Men parkda sayr qilishni va daraxtlarni ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu yaxshi, chunki u yerda tinch. Men gullarni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, tabiatda vaqt o'tkazishni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, bu juda dam beradi.
Masalan, uyimning yaqinidagi o'rmonda sayr qilishni yaxshi ko'raman. Shahardan uzoqlashish yaxshi.
Lekin, ba'zida juda ko'p hasharotlar bo'ladi!
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ha, men tabiatda vaqt o'tkazishni albatta yoqtiraman. Men buni juda tiklovchi deb bilaman. Daraxtlar va toza havo bilan o'ralgan bo'lish menga stressdan xalos bo'lishga va texnologiyadan uzilishga yordam beradi.
Masalan, men oyiga kamida bir marta piyoda sayr qilishga harakat qilaman. Charchatishi mumkin bo'lsa-da, erishilganlik hissi va go'zal manzaralar har doim bunga arziydi. Menimcha, yashil hududlarga ega bo'lish sog'lom turmush tarzini saqlash uchun juda muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Do you enjoy spending time in nature?
idioms: "Nature is the best medicine" - "Tabiat eng yaxshi davo"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I absolutely love spending time in nature because..." - "Ha, men tabiatda vaqt o'tkazishni juda yaxshi ko'raman, chunki..."
"Being in nature helps me to..." - "Tabiatda bo'lish menga ... yordam beradi..."
"I find natural environments very..." - "Men tabiiy muhitni juda ... deb topaman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I absolutely love spending time in nature. There's something incredibly refreshing about being surrounded by greenery, breathing fresh air, and escaping the hustle and bustle of city life.
Whenever I get the chance, I enjoy going for walks in parks or hiking in the mountains. I find that being in nature helps me clear my head and reduce stress. It's like a natural therapy that recharges my batteries.
I particularly love the sounds of nature – birds singing, leaves rustling, water flowing. These sounds are so peaceful compared to the noise of traffic and construction. As the saying goes, "Nature is the best medicine." I genuinely believe that spending time outdoors is essential for our mental well-being.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men tabiatda vaqt o'tkazishni juda yaxshi ko'raman. Yashillik bilan o'ralgan bo'lish, toza havodan nafas olish va shahar hayotining shovqinidan qochishda juda tetiklantiruvchi bir narsa bor.

Imkoniyat bo'lganda, bog'larda sayr qilishni yoki tog'larda piyoda yurishni yoqtiraman. Tabiatda bo'lish fikrlarimni tozalashga va stressni kamaytirishga yordam beradi. Bu xuddi batareyalarimni qayta zaryadlovchi tabiiy terapiya kabi.

Men ayniqsa tabiatning tovushlarini yaxshi ko'raman – qushlarning sayrashi, barglarning shivirashi, suvning oqishi. Bu tovushlar transport va qurilish shovqiniga nisbatan juda tinch. Aytishlaricha, "Tabiat eng yaxshi dori". Men chin dildan ochiq havoda vaqt o'tkazish bizning ruhiy salomatligimiz uchun zarur deb hisoblayman.

questions.prompt: What environmental issues concern you most?
questions.sampleA2:
I worry about pollution.

It is bad for animals and people.

I don't like dirty water, and I want to help.
questions.sampleB1:
I am worried about pollution.

Especially air pollution, because it makes it hard to breathe.

Also, I think we need to recycle more.

It's important for the future. For example, we can use less plastic.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose the thing that worries me most is plastic pollution. It's honestly everywhere these days, and it ends up in our rivers and oceans. Climate change is a massive concern too, to be fair. If we don't take action soon, I reckon future generations will really pay the price.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Atrof-muhitning ifloslanishi yomon.

Menga toza havo yoqadi.

Daraxtlar yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Meni ifloslanish tashvishga soladi.

Bu hayvonlar va odamlar uchun yomon.

Menga iflos suv yoqmaydi va men yordam berishni xohlayman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men ifloslanishdan xavotirdaman.

Ayniqsa, havo ifloslanishi, chunki bu nafas olishni qiyinlashtiradi.

Shuningdek, menimcha, biz ko'proq qayta ishlashimiz kerak.

Bu kelajak uchun muhim. Misol uchun, biz kamroq plastikdan foydalanishimiz mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Meni bir nechta ekologik muammolar tashvishga soladi, lekin o'ylashimcha, o'rmonlarning kesilishi ayniqsa xavotirli.

O'rmonlarning yo'qolishi iqlim o'zgarishiga hissa qo'shadi va ko'plab hayvonlarning yashash joylarini yo'q qiladi.

Shuningdek, u biz nafas olayotgan havoga ham ta'sir qiladi, chunki daraxtlar karbonat angidridni yutadi.

Bundan tashqari, biz ishlab chiqaradigan chiqindilar miqdori, ayniqsa plastmassa meni tashvishga soladi. Biz resurslarimizni boshqarish va atrof-muhitga ta'sirimizni kamaytirish uchun yanada barqaror usullarni topishimiz kerak.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - What environmental issues concern you most?
sentenceStarters: "The environmental issue that concerns me most is..." - "Meni eng ko'p tashvishga soladigan ekologik muammo..."
"I'm particularly worried about..." - "Men ayniqsa ... haqida xavotirdaman..."
"We're already seeing the effects of..." - "Biz allaqachon ... ning ta'sirini ko'rmoqdamiz..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
The environmental issue that concerns me most is undoubtedly climate change. It's a global crisis that affects every aspect of our lives and threatens the future of our planet.
We're already seeing the effects – more extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and species going extinct at alarming rates. What worries me most is that future generations will inherit a planet that's significantly worse than what we have today.
I'm also deeply concerned about plastic pollution. Our oceans are filled with plastic waste that harms marine life and eventually enters our food chain. It's heartbreaking to see images of animals suffering because of our carelessness. As they say, "We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children." We need to act now.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Meni eng ko'p tashvishga soladigan ekologik muammo, shubhasiz, iqlim o'zgarishi. Bu hayotimizning har bir jabhasiga ta'sir qiladigan va sayyoramiz kelajagiga tahdid soladigan global inqirozdir.

Biz allaqachon uning oqibatlarini ko'rmoqdamiz – yanada ekstremal ob-havo hodisalari, dengiz sathining ko'tarilishi va turlarning xavotirli darajada yo'q bo'lib ketishi. Meni eng ko'p tashvishga soladigan narsa shundaki, kelajak avlodlar biz bugun ega bo'lganimizdan ancha yomonroq sayyorani meros qilib olishadi.

Men, shuningdek, plastik ifloslanishi haqida ham juda tashvishdaman. Okeanlarimiz dengiz hayotiga zarar yetkazadigan va oxir-oqibat oziq-ovqat zanjirimizga kiradigan plastik chiqindilar bilan to'lib-toshgan. Bizning beparvoligimiz tufayli azob chekayotgan hayvonlarning rasmlarini ko'rish juda achinarli. Aytishlaricha, "Biz Yerni ota-bobolarimizdan meros qilib olmaymiz; biz uni farzandlarimizdan qarzga olamiz." Biz hozir harakat qilishimiz kerak.

questions.prompt: Do you try to recycle or reduce waste?
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I try. I recycle paper and bottles. And I don't buy many plastic bags because they are bad.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I try to recycle. I think it's important for the environment. For example, I recycle paper and plastic at home. However, sometimes it's difficult because there are not enough recycling bins near my house. So I try, but it's not always easy.
questions.sampleB2: Yeah, definitely — I try to do my bit where I can. At home, we sort out our rubbish into paper, glass and plastic. I've also started cutting down on single-use plastics by carrying a reusable bottle. It's a small effort, honestly, but I firmly believe every little helps.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha, men qayta ishlayman. Qog'oz va plastik.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, men harakat qilaman. Men qog'oz va butilkalarni qayta ishlayman. Va men ko'p plastik paketlar sotib olmayman, chunki ular yomon.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ha, men qayta ishlashga harakat qilaman. Menimcha, bu atrof-muhit uchun muhim. Masalan, men uyda qog'oz va plastmassani qayta ishlayman. Biroq, ba'zan qiyin bo'ladi, chunki uyimning yaqinida yetarli miqdorda qayta ishlash qutilari yo'q. Shuning uchun men harakat qilaman, lekin har doim ham oson emas.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men har doim imkon qadar chiqindilarni qayta ishlashga va kamaytirishga ongli ravishda harakat qilaman. Menimcha, bu umumiy mas'uliyat va hatto individual odatlardagi kichik o'zgarishlar ham birgalikda ijobiy ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkin. Misol uchun, men uyimning chiqindilarini diqqat bilan ajrataman va haddan tashqari qadoqlangan mahsulotlarni sotib olishdan qochaman. Bundan tashqari, men oziq-ovqat qoldiqlarini kompost qilishni boshladim, bu esa poligonlarga yuboradigan organik chiqindilar miqdorini sezilarli darajada kamaytirdi. Men mukammal emasman, lekin doimo atrof-muhitga ta'sirimni yaxshilash yo'llarini qidiraman.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you try to recycle or reduce waste?
idioms: "Every little helps" - "Har bir kichik narsa yordam beradi"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I definitely try to recycle by..." - "Ha, men albatta qayta ishlashga harakat qilaman..."
"I believe small actions can make a difference, such as..." - "Kichik harakatlar farq qilishi mumkin deb o'ylayman, masalan..."
"At home, I separate my waste into..." - "Uyda men chiqindilarimni ... ga ajrataman..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I definitely try to recycle and reduce waste as much as possible. I believe that small actions can make a big difference when everyone participates.
At home, I separate my waste into different categories – paper, plastic, glass, and organic waste. I also try to avoid single-use plastics by carrying my own reusable shopping bags and water bottle. It's a small inconvenience that's totally worth it.
Additionally, I try to cut down on unnecessary purchases and buy second-hand items when possible. Before throwing anything away, I ask myself if it can be reused or donated. As the saying goes, "Reduce, reuse, recycle." I think everyone should do their bit for the environment – every little helps!
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men albatta imkon qadar chiqindilarni qayta ishlashga va kamaytirishga harakat qilaman. Menimcha, har bir inson ishtirok etsa, kichik harakatlar ham katta farq qilishi mumkin.

Uyda men chiqindilarimni turli toifalarga ajrataman – qog'oz, plastik, shisha va organik chiqindilar. Shuningdek, o'zimning qayta ishlatiladigan xarid qilish sumkalarim va suv idishimni olib yurish orqali bir martalik plastiklardan qochishga harakat qilaman. Bu kichik noqulaylik, lekin bunga arziydi.

Bundan tashqari, men keraksiz xaridlarni qisqartirishga va imkon qadar ikkinchi qo'l buyumlarini sotib olishga harakat qilaman. Biror narsani tashlashdan oldin, o'zimdan uni qayta ishlatish yoki xayriya qilish mumkinmi, deb so'rayman. Aytishlaricha, "Kamaytir, qayta ishlat, qayta ishla". Menimcha, har bir inson atrof-muhit uchun o'z hissasini qo'shishi kerak – har qanday kichik yordam ham foydali!

questions.prompt: Compare these two pictures showing different environments.
questions.sampleA1:
Picture one, trees. Green. Good.

Picture two, smoke. Bad.
questions.sampleA2:
I see two pictures. One picture has trees and it is green. And the other picture has smoke and buildings.

The trees are good, but the smoke is bad for the air.
questions.sampleB1:
Okay, in the first picture, there are many trees and it looks like a forest. It seems very peaceful and clean.

However, the second picture is different. There are factories and a lot of smoke. I think it's bad for the environment.

The first picture is better because it's natural.
questions.sampleB2: These two pictures present a stark contrast in their depiction of the environment. The first image shows a woman enjoying a peaceful hike in a lush, dense forest, surrounded by tall trees and moss. It truly captures the serenity of nature. In stark contrast, the second picture portrays a grim scene of severe environmental degradation. We see a heavily polluted river filled with rubbish and industrial waste, with factories in the background emitting thick smoke. Radiation warning signs highlight the hazardous conditions. It's a powerful comparison between nature's beauty and human impact.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Birinchi rasm, daraxtlar. Yashil. Yaxshi.

Ikkinchi rasm, tutun. Yomon.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Men ikkita rasm ko'ryapman. Birinchi rasmda daraxtlar bor va u yashil. Va ikkinchi rasmda tutun va binolar bor.

Daraxtlar yaxshi, lekin tutun havo uchun yomon.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda ko'plab daraxtlar bor va u o'rmonga o'xshaydi. U juda tinch va toza ko'rinadi.

Biroq, ikkinchi rasm boshqacha. U yerda fabrikalar va ko'p tutun bor. Menimcha, bu atrof-muhit uchun yomon.

Birinchi rasm yaxshiroq, chunki u tabiiy.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Bu ikki rasm aniq ko'rsatib turibdiki, ular bir-biridan farq qiluvchi muhitlarni aks ettirmoqda. Birinchisi, ehtimol, o'rmon yoki park bo'lgan tabiiy manzarani tasvirlaydi, unda ko'plab ko'katlar va toza havo mavjud.

Ikkinchisi esa, tutun chiqaradigan fabrikalar bilan sanoat hududini ko'rsatadi, bu esa ifloslanishdan dalolat beradi. Farq juda sezilarli.

Shunday ko'rinadiki, bir rasm sog'lom muhitni ko'rsatadi, ikkinchisi esa sanoatning salbiy ta'sirini ochib beradi. Bu atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishni hisobga olish muhimligini ta'kidlaydi.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - Compare these two pictures...
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi"
sentenceStarters: "The first picture shows a beautiful..." - "Birinchi rasm go'zal ... ko'rsatmoqda..."
"In contrast, the second image depicts..." - "Aksincha, ikkinchi rasm ... tasvirlaydi..."
"These images illustrate the difference between..." - "Bu rasmlar ... o'rtasidagi farqni ko'rsatadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures present a stark contrast between two very different environments that exist in our world today.
The first image shows a pristine natural environment. We can see lush greenery, clean air, and a peaceful atmosphere. This type of environment represents what nature looks like when it's properly protected and preserved. It's the kind of place where people go to relax, breathe fresh air, and connect with nature. The scene looks incredibly calming and inviting.
In contrast, the second image depicts a heavily polluted industrial area. We can see smokestacks releasing emissions into the air, creating a grey, hazy atmosphere. This environment looks distinctly unhealthy and unwelcoming. The air quality is obviously poor, and it's hard to imagine people living comfortably in such conditions.
These images powerfully illustrate the environmental choices we face as a society. One shows what we could preserve, while the other shows the consequences of unchecked industrialization. As they say, "A picture is worth a thousand words," and these two pictures tell a very important story about our planet's future.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm bugungi kunda dunyomizda mavjud bo'lgan ikki xil muhit o'rtasida keskin farqni ko'rsatadi.

Birinchi rasmda toza tabiiy muhit tasvirlangan. Biz serhosil ko'katlar, toza havo va tinch muhitni ko'rishimiz mumkin. Bu turdagi muhit tabiat to'g'ri himoyalangan va saqlanganida qanday ko'rinishga ega ekanligini aks ettiradi. Bu odamlar dam olish, toza havodan nafas olish va tabiat bilan bog'lanish uchun boradigan joy. Manzara juda sokin va jozibali ko'rinadi.

Aksincha, ikkinchi rasmda kuchli ifloslangan sanoat hududi tasvirlangan. Biz tutun chiqaradigan mo'rilarning havoga chiqarayotgan chiqindilarini ko'rishimiz mumkin, bu esa kulrang, tumanli muhitni yaratadi. Bu muhit aniq nosog'lom va yoqimsiz ko'rinadi. Havo sifati, shubhasiz, yomon va bunday sharoitda odamlarning qulay yashashini tasavvur qilish qiyin.

Bu rasmlar jamiyat sifatida duch kelayotgan ekologik tanlovlarimizni kuchli tarzda ko'rsatib beradi. Birinchisi biz nimalarni saqlab qolishimiz mumkinligini ko'rsatsa, ikkinchisi nazoratsiz sanoatlashtirish oqibatlarini ko'rsatadi. Aytganlaridek, "Bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi" va bu ikki rasm sayyoramizning kelajagi haqida juda muhim hikoyani aytib beradi.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of spending time in clean, natural places?
questions.sampleA2:
I like park. It is clean.

I can walk and see trees and flowers.

It is good for me because I am happy and I can relax.
questions.sampleB1:
I think it's good to go to natural places.

For example, parks or forests are very nice.

It's good because the air is clean and you can relax there.

Also, I think it's good for your health because you can walk and exercise.
questions.sampleB2: Well, I think there are loads of benefits, to be honest. First off, the fresh air does wonders for your body. On top of that, being in nature really helps you switch off and de-stress after a hectic week. It's also a great excuse to get some exercise, which is brilliant for your overall wellbeing.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Menga park yoqadi. U toza.

Men u yerda sayr qilib, daraxtlar va gullarni ko'rishim mumkin.

Bu men uchun yaxshi, chunki men xursand bo'laman va dam olishim mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, tabiiy joylarga borish yaxshi.

Masalan, parklar yoki o'rmonlar juda yaxshi.

Bu yaxshi, chunki havo toza va u yerda dam olishingiz mumkin.

Shuningdek, menimcha, bu sizning sog'lig'ingiz uchun yaxshi, chunki siz piyoda yurishingiz va mashq qilishingiz mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Tabiatda vaqt o'tkazishning, albatta, ko'plab afzalliklari bor.

Birinchidan, bu stressni kamaytirish va ruhiy holatingizni yaxshilashning ajoyib usuli.

Yashil hududlar bilan o'ralgan bo'lish juda tinchlantiruvchi bo'lishi va kundalik bosimlardan uzoqlashishingizga yordam berishi mumkin.

Shuningdek, u jismoniy faollikni rag'batlantiradi, bu sizning umumiy salomatligingiz uchun foydali.

Bundan tashqari, u atrof-muhitga bo'lgan minnatdorchiligingizni oshirishi va uni himoya qilishga undashi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of spending time in natural places?
idioms: "A breath of fresh air" - "Toza havo nafasi"
sentenceStarters: "One of the main benefits is..." - "Asosiy afzalliklardan biri..."
"Being in nature helps us to..." - "Tabiatda bo'lish bizga ... yordam beradi..."
"Studies have shown that natural environments..." - "Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatdiki, tabiiy muhit..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Spending time in clean, natural environments offers numerous significant benefits for both our physical and mental health.
Firstly, being in nature provides us with fresh, clean air to breathe. Unlike polluted cities, natural areas have air that's rich in oxygen and free from harmful pollutants. This is particularly beneficial for our respiratory system and overall health.
Secondly, nature has proven mental health benefits. Studies show that spending just 20 minutes in a natural setting can significantly reduce stress hormones and lower blood pressure. The peaceful surroundings help us switch off from daily worries and find inner calm.
Additionally, natural environments encourage physical activity. Whether it's hiking, swimming, or simply walking, we tend to move more when surrounded by beautiful scenery. This helps combat the sedentary lifestyle that many of us lead.
Furthermore, connecting with nature fosters a sense of environmental awareness. When we experience the beauty of clean environments, we're more motivated to protect them. As the proverb says, "In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks."
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Toza, tabiiy muhitda vaqt o'tkazish jismoniy va ruhiy salomatligimiz uchun ko'plab muhim foydalarni taqdim etadi.

Birinchidan, tabiatda bo'lish bizga nafas olish uchun toza havoni beradi. Ifloslangan shaharlardan farqli o'laroq, tabiiy hududlarda kislorodga boy va zararli ifloslantiruvchi moddalardan xoli havo mavjud. Bu, ayniqsa, nafas olish tizimimiz va umumiy salomatligimiz uchun foydalidir.

Ikkinchidan, tabiatning ruhiy salomatlik uchun foydalari isbotlangan. Tadqiqotlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, tabiiy muhitda atigi 20 daqiqa vaqt o'tkazish stress gormonlarini sezilarli darajada kamaytirishi va qon bosimini pasaytirishi mumkin. Tinch muhit bizga kundalik tashvishlardan chalg'ishga va ichki xotirjamlikni topishga yordam beradi.

Bundan tashqari, tabiiy muhit jismoniy faollikni rag'batlantiradi. Piyoda yurish, suzish yoki shunchaki sayr qilish bo'ladimi, biz go'zal manzaralar bilan o'ralganimizda ko'proq harakat qilishga moyilmiz. Bu ko'pchiligimiz olib boradigan harakatsiz turmush tarziga qarshi kurashishga yordam beradi.

Bundan tashqari, tabiat bilan bog'lanish atrof-muhitga nisbatan xabardorlik tuyg'usini kuchaytiradi. Toza muhitning go'zalligini his qilganimizda, biz ularni himoya qilishga ko'proq motivatsiya olamiz. Maqolda aytilganidek, "Tabiat bilan har bir sayrda inson o'zi izlaganidan ko'ra ko'proq narsaga erishadi."

questions.prompt: Why do some cities struggle with pollution problems?
questions.sampleA1: City have pollution. Cars many. Factory many. Air not good.
questions.sampleA2: Some cities have pollution because there are many cars. And factories make pollution too. It is bad for the air and people get sick.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think some cities have pollution problems because there are a lot of cars and factories. For example, in big cities, there's a lot of traffic, so the air isn't very clean. Also, sometimes the factories make smoke and bad things, and that makes the pollution worse.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the thing is, a lot of it comes down to rapid industrialisation. As cities grow, factories and cars pump out huge amounts of emissions. On top of that, poor public transport means everyone relies on their own car. And to be honest, weak environmental regulations often let industries get away with it.
questions.uzSampleA1: Shaharlarda ifloslanish bor. Mashinalar ko'p. Zavodlar ko'p. Havo yaxshi emas.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ba'zi shaharlarda ifloslanish bor, chunki u yerda ko'p mashinalar bor. Va fabrikalar ham ifloslanishni keltirib chiqaradi. Bu havo uchun yomon va odamlar kasal bo'lib qoladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha, ba'zi shaharlarda ifloslanish muammolari bor, chunki u yerda juda ko'p mashinalar va fabrikalar bor.
Masalan, katta shaharlarda tirbandlik juda ko'p, shuning uchun havo unchalik toza emas.
Shuningdek, ba'zida fabrikalar tutun va yomon narsalarni chiqaradi va bu ifloslanishni yanada kuchaytiradi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ba'zi shaharlarda ifloslanish muammolariga bir nechta omillar sabab bo'ladi. Asosiy sabablardan biri ko'pincha tez urbanizatsiya va sanoat o'sishi bo'lib, bu zavodlar va transport vositalaridan chiqadigan chiqindilarning ko'payishiga olib keladi. Yana bir muhim omil - infratuzilmaning yetarli emasligi, ayniqsa jamoat transporti va chiqindilarni boshqarish sohasida. Samarali jamoat transportisiz ko'proq odamlar shaxsiy avtomobillarga tayanadi, bu esa havo ifloslanishini yanada kuchaytiradi. Bundan tashqari, samarasiz ekologik qoidalar yoki ularning yetarli darajada ta'minlanmaganligi sanoat korxonalariga hech qanday oqibatlarsiz atrof-muhitni ifloslantirishga imkon berishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some cities struggle with pollution problems?
idioms: you can't have your cake and eat it too - "ikki quyonni birdan tutib bo'lmaydi"
sentenceStarters: "Many cities struggle with pollution because..." - "Ko'p shaharlar ifloslanish bilan kurashmoqda, chunki..."
"Rapid industrialization has led to..." - "Tez industrializatsiya ... ga olib keldi..."
"Poor waste management contributes to..." - "Chiqindilarni yomon boshqarish ... ga hissa qo'shadi..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many cities around the world struggle with severe pollution problems due to a combination of factors.
Firstly, rapid industrialization is a major cause. As cities develop and factories are built, they often release harmful emissions into the air and water. In many developing countries, environmental regulations are either weak or poorly enforced, allowing industries to pollute freely.
Secondly, the sheer number of vehicles on the roads contributes significantly to air pollution. As populations grow and more people can afford cars, traffic congestion increases, and so do exhaust emissions. Many cities lack adequate public transportation systems, forcing people to rely on private vehicles.
Additionally, poor waste management is a serious issue. In some cities, garbage is not collected regularly or is disposed of improperly. This leads to overflowing landfills and even waste being burned openly, releasing toxic fumes.
Furthermore, economic priorities often overshadow environmental concerns. Governments may prioritize economic growth over environmental protection, viewing pollution as an acceptable cost of development. As they say, "You can't have your cake and eat it too" – but perhaps with better planning, cities can achieve both growth and sustainability.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Dunyo bo'ylab ko'plab shaharlar bir qator omillar tufayli jiddiy ifloslanish muammolari bilan kurashmoqda.

Birinchidan, jadal sanoatlashuv asosiy sababdir. Shaharlar rivojlanib, fabrikalar qurilgan sari, ular ko'pincha havoga va suvga zararli chiqindilarni chiqaradi. Ko'pgina rivojlanayotgan mamlakatlarda atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish qoidalari yoki zaif, yoki yaxshi amalga oshirilmaydi, bu esa sanoat korxonalariga erkin ifloslantirish imkonini beradi.

Ikkinchidan, yo'llardagi transport vositalarining soni havo ifloslanishiga sezilarli darajada hissa qo'shadi. Aholi soni o'sib, ko'proq odamlar mashina sotib olishga qodir bo'lgani sari, tirbandlik ortadi va shunga mos ravishda chiqindi gazlari ham ko'payadi. Ko'pgina shaharlarda jamoat transporti tizimlari yetarli emas, bu esa odamlarni shaxsiy transport vositalariga tayanishga majbur qiladi.

Bundan tashqari, chiqindilarni noto'g'ri boshqarish jiddiy muammodir. Ba'zi shaharlarda axlat muntazam ravishda yig'ishtirilmaydi yoki noto'g'ri utilizatsiya qilinadi. Bu esa to'lib-toshgan poligonlarga va hatto chiqindilarning ochiqchasiga yoqilishiga olib keladi, natijada zaharli tutunlar tarqaladi.

Bundan tashqari, iqtisodiy ustuvorliklar ko'pincha atrof-muhitga oid tashvishlarni soyada qoldiradi. Hukumatlar iqtisodiy o'sishni atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishdan ustun qo'yishi, ifloslanishni rivojlanishning maqbul narxi deb hisoblashi mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Bir vaqtning o'zida ham qovoqni yeyish, ham urug'ini saqlab qolishning iloji yo'q" – lekin ehtimol, yaxshiroq rejalashtirish bilan shaharlar ham o'sishga, ham barqarorlikka erishishi mumkin.

questions.prompt: Describe a beautiful natural place you have visited.
questions.sampleA1: I went to park. It is nice. Trees are green. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: I went to the beach last summer. It was very sunny and hot. I swam in the sea and I played with my brother. I liked it a lot because it was fun.
questions.sampleB1: I went to the mountains last year. It was a really beautiful place. I think the best thing was the view from the top. You could see everything. Also, the air was very clean. I would like to go there again someday.
questions.sampleB2: Right, I'd like to tell you about a trip I took to Charvak Lake, which is honestly one of the most breathtaking places I've ever laid eyes on. It's a huge reservoir tucked away in the mountains, roughly eighty kilometres from Tashkent, and I went there with my family a couple of summers ago. The thing is, the journey itself was half the magic. As we wound our way up the mountain roads, the scenery just kept getting better and better, and by the time the lake came into view, it genuinely took my breath away. The water was this incredible turquoise colour, completely crystal clear, and it was framed by these towering, rugged mountains on every side. What made it so memorable, I suppose, was the sheer peace and quiet. Back in the city you're surrounded by noise and traffic, but up there all you could hear was the water lapping against the shore. Honestly, you could happily wander along the shoreline for hours and lose all track of time. We spent the whole day swimming, having a picnic by the water's edge, and just soaking up the natural beauty around us. The air felt so fresh and clean compared to home. To be honest, being there left me feeling completely at peace — all my worries seemed to melt away. It also brought home to me just how important it is to look after these places. I'd recommend it to anyone without hesitation; it's the kind of spot that really stays with you long after you've left.

Suv juda tiniq edi, atrofdagi o'rmonlar esa serhosil va yashil edi. Meni eng ko'p hayratga solgani bu joyning osoyishtaligi edi; siz shunchaki yog'och yo'laklar bo'ylab sayr qilib, suvning ovozini tinglashingiz mumkin edi. Bu juda tetiklantiruvchi tajriba edi va men buni tabiatda bo'lishni yoqtiradigan har bir kishiga tavsiya qilaman.

bulletPoints: Describe a beautiful natural place you have visited.
Where is this place and when did you visit?
What made it special or memorable?
questions.sampleAnswer:
I'd like to describe a visit to Charvak Lake in Uzbekistan, which remains one of the most breathtaking natural places I've ever seen.
I visited Charvak during the summer holidays about two years ago with my family. It's a large artificial reservoir located in the mountains, about 80 kilometers from Tashkent. The journey itself was incredibly scenic, winding through mountain roads with spectacular views at every turn.
What made this place truly special was the combination of crystal-clear turquoise water surrounded by majestic mountains. The contrast between the blue lake and the green and brown mountains was absolutely stunning. We spent the day swimming, having a picnic by the shore, and simply admiring the natural beauty around us. The air was so fresh and clean compared to the city.
Being there made me feel completely at peace. All my worries seemed to disappear as I took in the magnificent scenery. I felt a deep sense of gratitude for such natural wonders. It reminded me why we need to protect these places. As they say, "The Earth has music for those who listen." That day, I truly heard it.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men O'zbekistondagi Chorvoq ko'liga tashrifim haqida gapirmoqchiman, u men ko'rgan eng hayratlanarli tabiiy joylardan biri bo'lib qolmoqda.

Men Chorvoqqa taxminan ikki yil oldin yozgi ta'tilda oilam bilan borganman. Bu Toshkentdan taxminan 80 kilometr uzoqlikda, tog'larda joylashgan katta sun'iy suv ombori. Sayohatning o'zi juda go'zal edi, har burilishda ajoyib manzaralar bilan tog' yo'llari bo'ylab o'tadi.

Bu joyni haqiqatan ham o'zgacha qilgan narsa - ulug'vor tog'lar bilan o'ralgan tiniq turkuaz suvning kombinatsiyasi edi. Moviy ko'l va yashil va jigarrang tog'lar o'rtasidagi kontrast juda ajoyib edi. Biz kunni suzish, qirg'oq bo'yida piknik qilish va shunchaki atrofimizdagi tabiiy go'zallikka qoyil qolish bilan o'tkazdik. Havo shaharga nisbatan juda toza va musaffo edi.

U yerda bo'lish meni butunlay xotirjam his qildirdi. Ajoyib manzarani tomosha qilar ekanman, barcha tashvishlarim yo'qolgandek bo'ldi. Bunday tabiiy mo'jizalar uchun chuqur minnatdorchilik hissini tuyg'dim. Bu bizga bunday joylarni nega himoya qilishimiz kerakligini eslatdi. Aytishlaricha, "Yer tinglay oladiganlar uchun musiqa yaratgan". O'sha kuni men buni chinakam his qildim.

questions.prompt: Governments Should Prioritize Environmental Protection Over Economic Growth
questions.sampleA1: Environment good. Money good too. But environment more important. I like trees.
questions.sampleA2: I think environment is important. Money is important too, but we need clean air and water. And if we don't have a good environment, we can't live. So, environment is maybe more important because we need it.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think the environment is very important. It's important for our health and for the future. Economic growth is also important, of course, because people need jobs. However, I think we need to find a balance. For example, we can have green jobs that help the environment and also help the economy.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is a really interesting topic, and to be honest I can see arguments on both sides. On the one hand, I completely understand why some people put economic growth first. At the end of the day, a strong economy creates jobs, lifts people out of poverty and pays for things like schools and hospitals. In developing countries especially, you could argue that raising living standards has to come first, because it's hard to worry about the environment when people are struggling to make ends meet. On the other hand, though, I firmly believe that protecting the environment should be the priority in the long run. The thing is, economic growth means very little if the planet becomes unliveable. Problems like climate change, air pollution and resource depletion don't just go away — they build up over time and end up costing us far more to fix. We're already starting to see the consequences, from extreme weather to rising sea levels. As the saying goes, we can't have our cake and eat it too, at least not forever. Personally, I don't think it has to be an either-or situation, to be fair. I reckon the smartest approach is to invest in green technologies and renewable energy, which actually create jobs while protecting the planet at the same time. Countries like Denmark have shown that going green and growing the economy can actually go hand in hand. So all in all, while the economy obviously matters, I'd argue that long-term sustainability should always win out in the end.
questions.uzSampleA1: Atrof-muhit yaxshi. Pul ham yaxshi. Lekin atrof-muhit muhimroq. Menga daraxtlar yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, atrof-muhit muhim. Pul ham muhim, lekin bizga toza havo va suv kerak. Agar bizda yaxshi atrof-muhit bo'lmasa, biz yashay olmaymiz. Shunday ekan, atrof-muhit balki muhimroqdir, chunki bizga u kerak.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, menimcha atrof-muhit juda muhim. Bu bizning sog'lig'imiz va kelajagimiz uchun muhim. Iqtisodiy o'sish ham, albatta, muhim, chunki odamlarga ish kerak.
Ammo, menimcha, biz muvozanatni topishimiz kerak.
Masalan, bizda atrof-muhitga yordam beradigan va iqtisodiyotga ham yordam beradigan "yashil" ish o'rinlari bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Hukumatlar atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishni iqtisodiy o'sishdan ustun qo'yishi kerakmi degan savol murakkab masala. Iqtisodiy o'sish ish o'rinlarini yaratish va turmush darajasini yaxshilash uchun muhim bo'lsa-da, menimcha, atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishga ko'proq e'tibor qaratish kerak. Axir, sog'lom atrof-muhit uzoq muddatli barqarorlik uchun zarurdir. To'g'ri, atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish qoidalari ba'zan qisqa muddatda iqtisodiy o'sishga to'sqinlik qilishi mumkin.
Biroq, atrof-muhitga yetkazilgan zararning uzoq muddatli xarajatlari, masalan, iqlim o'zgarishi va resurslarning kamayishi ancha yuqori. Shuning uchun, hukumatlar atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish va barqaror iqtisodiy rivojlanishni rag'batlantiradigan yashil texnologiyalar va siyosatlarga investitsiya kiritishi kerak.

vocabulary.title: Q8 - Governments Should Prioritize Environmental Protection Over Economic Growth
idioms: "You reap what you sow" - "Nima eksang, shuni o'rasan"
a drop in the ocean - "dengizda bir tomchi"
sentenceStarters: "On the one hand, environmental protection is crucial because..." - "Bir tomondan, atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish juda muhim, chunki..."
"On the other hand, economic growth is necessary for..." - "Boshqa tomondan, iqtisodiy o'sish ... uchun zarur..."
"I believe we need to find a balance between..." - "Menimcha, biz ... o'rtasida muvozanat topishimiz kerak..."

for: Climate change threatens human survival – nothing is more important
Environmental damage is often irreversible once done
Green industries can create new jobs and economic opportunities
against: Economic growth lifts people out of poverty
Environmental regulations can cause job losses in traditional industries
Technology and innovation can solve environmental problems without sacrificing growth

questions.sampleAnswer:
The debate over whether governments should prioritize environmental protection over economic growth is one of the most pressing issues of our time. Let me examine both perspectives.
Those who argue for prioritizing the environment make several compelling points. Firstly, climate change poses an existential threat to humanity – what good is economic growth if our planet becomes uninhabitable? Secondly, environmental damage is often irreversible. Once forests are destroyed or species go extinct, they're gone forever. Additionally, clean air and water are basic human rights – no amount of money can compensate for health problems caused by pollution. Furthermore, the transition to green industries can actually create millions of new jobs in renewable energy, sustainable agriculture, and eco-tourism.
On the other hand, opponents argue that economic growth is essential for improving people's lives. In developing nations, industry provides jobs and lifts families out of poverty. Strict environmental regulations could cause unemployment and economic hardship. Some believe that technological innovation will eventually solve environmental problems without sacrificing growth. They also point out that countries restricting industry will simply lose business to less regulated competitors.
In my view, this shouldn't be an either-or choice. Sustainable development – economic growth that doesn't harm the environment – should be the goal. As the proverb wisely states, "We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children." We must find a balance that ensures both prosperity and a healthy planet.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Hukumatlar atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilishni iqtisodiy o'sishdan ustun qo'yishlari kerakmi yoki yo'qmi degan bahs, bizning davrimizning eng dolzarb masalalaridan biridir. Keling, har ikki nuqtai nazarni ko'rib chiqaylik.

Atrof-muhitni ustun qo'yish tarafdorlari bir nechta ishonchli dalillarni keltiradilar. Birinchidan, iqlim o'zgarishi insoniyat uchun mavjudlik tahdidini soladi – agar sayyoramiz yashashga yaroqsiz bo'lsa, iqtisodiy o'sishdan nima foyda? Ikkinchidan, atrof-muhitga yetkazilgan zarar ko'pincha qaytarilmas bo'ladi. O'rmonlar yo'q qilingandan yoki turlar yo'q bo'lib ketgandan so'ng, ular abadiy yo'qoladi. Bundan tashqari, toza havo va suv insonning asosiy huquqlaridir – hech qanday pul ifloslanish natijasida kelib chiqqan sog'liq muammolarini qoplay olmaydi. Bundan tashqari, yashil sanoatga o'tish qayta tiklanadigan energiya, barqaror qishloq xo'jaligi va eko-turizmda millionlab yangi ish o'rinlarini yaratishi mumkin.

Boshqa tomondan, qarshilar iqtisodiy o'sish odamlarning hayotini yaxshilash uchun zarur deb ta'kidlaydilar. Rivojlanayotgan davlatlarda sanoat ish o'rinlari bilan ta'minlaydi va oilalarni qashshoqlikdan olib chiqadi. Atrof-muhitni muhofaza qilish bo'yicha qat'iy qoidalar ishsizlik va iqtisodiy qiyinchiliklarga olib kelishi mumkin. Ba'zilarning fikricha, texnologik innovatsiyalar oxir-oqibat o'sishni qurbon qilmasdan atrof-muhit muammolarini hal qiladi. Ular, shuningdek, sanoatni cheklaydigan davlatlar shunchaki kamroq tartibga solingan raqobatchilarga biznesni boy berishini ta'kidlaydilar.

Mening fikrimcha, bu yoki u tanlovi bo'lmasligi kerak. Barqaror rivojlanish – atrof-muhitga zarar yetkazmaydigan iqtisodiy o'sish – maqsad bo'lishi kerak. Maqolda aytilganidek, "Biz Yer yuzini ota-bobolarimizdan meros qilib olmaymiz; biz uni farzandlarimizdan qarzga olamiz." Biz ham farovonlikni, ham sog'lom sayyorani ta'minlaydigan muvozanatni topishimiz kerak.
